info.title: Leap Incentives — Programs
info.description: API for managing program definitions, requirement catalog, field groups, and partner data preferences

get.description: Browse Leap's catalog of rebate programs. The catalog is shared across partners, so a program you read here is not necessarily one your account can claim. Narrow it with `filter`, and page through it with `page_size` and `page_token`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Comma-separated `field=value` pairs, combined with AND. Supported fields: `program_type`, `transmission_region`, `enabled`, `device_category`, `customer_classification` and `state`. For example, `filter=program_type=VPP,enabled=true` returns the enabled programs that put a device under control.

An unrecognised field returns 400. `enabled` must be `true` or `false`; anything else returns 400. With no `enabled` filter the response mixes enabled and disabled programs, and each row carries its own `enabled` flag.

Repeat `device_category` or `customer_classification` to match any of several values: `device_category=ev_charger,device_category=solar_storage` matches either. A Leap program that names no device category or classification matches every value. Every other field keeps its last value if repeated.

`state` matches a program's own state when it has one. Otherwise it matches the state Leap records for each utility the program serves. All comparisons are case-insensitive.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Free-text search over each program's `label`, `program_identifier` and `metadata.operator_name`. Matching is case-insensitive and finds a word anywhere in those fields. Every word must match, so adding words narrows the result. Combines with `filter` and `exclude_source`.

A value over 200 characters returns 400. Leap reads the first 10 words, and the first 64 characters of each.

parameters.name: include_facets
parameters.description:
Set to `true` to add a `facets` object to the response. It counts the programs matching your `filter`, `q` and `exclude_source` across every page. It also breaks them down by device category, customer classification, state and program type.

Send it on the first page only: a request with both `include_facets=true` and a `page_token` returns 400. The counts describe the whole filtered listing, so they are the same on every page. Defaults to `false`.

parameters.name: exclude_source
parameters.description:
Comma-separated program sources to leave out: `LEAP_DEFINITIONS`, `INCENTIVES_DB` or `PARTNER_OFFER`. For example, `exclude_source=PARTNER_OFFER` lists catalog programs without any partner offers. An unrecognised value returns 400.

The exclusion applies to the listed programs and to the `facets` counts alike. Omit it to include every source.

get.description: Retrieve one program by its `program_identifier`, the same value **Look up incentives** returns on each eligible program. An identifier Leap does not hold returns 404.

List the Approved Product List (APL) entries for a program: the catalog devices it pays a rebate on. Each entry names the catalog `device_id`, the tier it is bound to when it is tier-specific, and the APL publication it came from. Resolve a `device_id` with **Search device catalog**.

ProgramIdentifier.name: programIdentifier
ProgramIdentifier.description: The program's `program_identifier`. This route spells the path segment `programIdentifier` while every other program route uses `program_id`; both take the same value.

PageToken.name: page_token
PageToken.description: Cursor from a previous response's `next_page_token`. Follow it until it is absent to walk the whole catalog. Replay a token only with the `filter` that produced it. Programs are ordered by `program_identifier`, so a program added below your cursor part-way through a walk is missed rather than duplicated. This route pages with `page_size` and `page_token` only: `limit` and `offset` return 400.

PageSize.name: page_size
PageSize.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 200; a larger value is clamped rather than rejected.

Unauthorized.description: You are not authorized to perform this operation

Forbidden.description: You do not have permission to perform this operation

NotFound.description: The requested resource was not found

RequirementSource.description: Where the definition came from. `LEAP_DEFINITIONS` and `INCENTIVES_DB` are rebate programs Leap maintains. `PARTNER_OFFER` marks a partner offer, which a partner account configures rather than Leap.

ProgramOperatorType.description: Who the customer enrolls through. `LEAP` marks Leap's own programs, even when a utility or grid operator runs the underlying program. `metadata.operator_name` names that operator. `PARTNER` marks every partner offer. `UTILITY`, `STATE`, `LOCAL`, `FEDERAL` and `PROVINCIAL` give the kind of public operator for every other catalog program. The field is omitted when Leap hasn't recorded an operator yet, which means unknown, not none. Treat an absent field and a null one the same way. `metadata.operator_type` keeps the stored lower-case value.

program_identifier.description: Stable identifier for the program, and the value **Look up incentives** returns as `program_identifier` on each eligible program. Send it as the `program_id` path segment on the other program routes.

program_type.description: Whether the program puts the customer's device under control. `VPP` means the customer enrolls the device in a program that controls or dispatches it. Demand response, managed charging and virtual power plant programs are all `VPP`. `REBATE` means the program pays toward buying or installing the device and doesn't control it afterwards. Read `operator_type` for who the customer enrolls through.

enabled.description: Whether Leap currently evaluates this program. A disabled program never appears in a lookup result. Filter on it with `filter=enabled=true` or `filter=enabled=false`.

metadata.description:
The partner-visible subset of the program's stored metadata. Responses carry an allowlist of keys rather than everything Leap stores against a program. Catalog description: `url`, `operator_name`, `operator_type`, `device_category`, `application_path`, `state_province`, `country`. Partner offer publication, present on `PARTNER_OFFER` rows: `display_name`, `operator_display_name`, `logo_url`, `terms_url`, `description`. Any other key is omitted, including keys added after this was written, and including a partner offer's private configuration. Present but empty when the program carries none of the twelve.

Values are constrained as well as names. An allowlisted key survives only when its value is a string, a number or a boolean; a key whose value is an object or an array is omitted, because a nested value can carry fields nobody reviewed. Strings longer than 2048 characters are omitted rather than truncated, so a value you receive is always the whole value. No stored value under the seven catalog keys comes close to that bound.

upstream_program_id.description:
The program's identifier in the upstream incentives system that owns application records. Stable, and the intended join key between this catalog and any API that reports a program in that id space, such as the applications feed. Always a positive integer, rendered as a string so the id stays exact for clients whose numbers are IEEE doubles.

Not to be confused with `source_program_identifier` on the eligibility-details response, which is a program identifier in *this* service's id space, attributing a check to the program that imposed it. The two never hold interchangeable values.

Omitted entirely when the program has no upstream counterpart, so treat an absent field and a null one the same way. That is normal rather than a gap: programs sourced from Leap's own definitions were never defined in the upstream system, so a missing id here says "this program cannot be joined", never "no applications exist". Programs promoted from that system, including partner offers, always carry one.

eiaids.description: Every EIA utility id this program serves. A customer qualifies on the utility dimension when the utility resolved from their address appears in this list. An empty list means the program has no utility footprint and is never selected on that dimension.

device_categories.description: Every device category the program covers. Leap offers the program to a customer with a device in any listed category, or in `device_category`. Empty when the program names only `device_category`.

ProgramSummaryResponse.description: One program in Leap's rebate catalog. The catalog is shared across partners and covers utility, state and market programs, so a program you read here is not necessarily one your account can claim.

next_page_token.description: Cursor for the next page, absent on the last page. Pass it back as `page_token`, with the same filter that produced it.

ProgramListResponse.description: One page of catalog programs, plus the cursor for the next page.

ProgramFacets.description:
Counts that describe the whole filtered listing, not only the page in `data`. Present only when the request sets `include_facets=true`.

Each per-value map is counted without its own filter field. A dropdown can then show what choosing another value would return. For example, `by_state` ignores your `state` filter and applies every other one. The maps therefore don't add up to `total`.

total.description: Programs matching the current filter, across every page.

enabled_count.description: How many of the `total` programs are enabled. Leap evaluates only enabled programs in a lookup.

by_device_category.description: Programs per device category, keyed by lower-case category and counted without your `device_category` filter. A Leap program that names no device category matches every category under a filter. It appears in no bucket here, and `wildcard_category_count` counts those programs.

by_customer_classification.description: Programs per customer classification, keyed by upper-case value and counted without your `customer_classification` filter. A Leap program that names no classification matches every classification under a filter. It appears in no bucket here, and `wildcard_classification_count` counts those programs.

by_state.description:
Programs per state, keyed by upper-case state code and counted without your `state` filter.

A program with its own state counts in that state. A program without one counts once in the state Leap records for each utility it serves. Leap records one state per utility, so a utility serving several states places its programs in one of them. A program with neither appears in no bucket.

by_program_type.description: Programs per `program_type`, such as `VPP` and `REBATE`, counted without your `program_type` filter. Each program counts once, so this map splits distinct programs by type. The state maps can't give that split, because they count a program once per state.

by_state_program_type.description: `by_state` split by `program_type`: keyed by state code, then by program type, to a count. For each state, the counts sum to that state's `by_state` value. Keys are the `program_type` values as stored, so a new type appears as its own key.

placed_program_count.description:
Distinct programs that appear in at least one `by_state` bucket. The sum of `by_state` counts a program once per state, so it is larger whenever a program spans states.

`total` minus this value is the number of matching programs Leap can't place in any state. It is counted under your whole filter, including `state`, so it covers the same programs as `total`.

wildcard_category_count.description: Leap programs that name no device category, so they match every category when you filter on one. They appear in no `by_device_category` bucket. Add this number to each bucket for per-category counts that agree with filtering. Counted without your `device_category` filter.

wildcard_classification_count.description: The same count for customer classification: Leap programs that name no classification, so they serve every customer segment. Add this number to each `by_customer_classification` bucket for counts that agree with filtering. Counted without your `customer_classification` filter.

device_id.description: Catalog device UUID. It is the same identifier **Search device catalog** returns as `id`, and the same one you send as `device_id` on a lookup.

tier_id.description: The incentive tier this device is bound to. Absent when the entry is not tier-specific.

apl_source.description: The Approved Product List publication this entry came from.

apl_version.description: The version of that Approved Product List publication.

ProgramApprovedDeviceResponse.description: One Approved Product List entry: a catalog device this program pays a rebate on.

CustomerClassification.description: The customer or site class this program serves. `RESIDENTIAL` and `COMMERCIAL` are the long-standing values; `MULTIFAMILY` and `MANUFACTURED_HOME` exist because rebate qualification differs across single-family, multifamily and manufactured housing.

BearerAuth.description: Your Leap API key as a Bearer token. Send it in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`.
